arms.diagnostic_note: The control's purpose (demonstrating the score is lower without break-and-extend) is confirmed: 81 < 83. The predicted score of 82 was incorrect — actual is 81, matching iter-2 findings (modal 81). The predicted test 10 k of ~21000 was far off (actual k=5088). The iter-2 findings never reported test 10 k precisely; the designer appears to have assumed the iter-2 solution reached ~21000 on test 10 but the actual iter-2 solution (Warnsdorff Phase 2, no max-degree restarts) reaches only 5088. The Phase 2 difference (Warnsdorff vs max-degree) accounts for the large k gap on both test 8 and test 10.

discrepancy_analysis: Both arms CONFIRMED directionally. h-main scored 83 (3/3 runs), h-control-negative scored 81 (3/3 runs). The +2 point gap consists of: (1) test 10 +1 point from break-and-extend (k=23713 vs 5088, crossing threshold 23333), and (2) test 8 +1 point from Phase 2 improvement (max-degree rapid restarts vs Warnsdorff slow restarts, k=5638 vs 3309, crossing threshold 4720). The designer predicted the improvement would come 'exclusively from test 10' but the iter-3 standard path's Phase 2 was also changed from the iter-2 solution, producing an undeclared test 8 improvement. The designer's predicted baseline of 82 was wrong (actual 81). The break-and-extend mechanism is clearly validated: test 10 k improved from 5088 to 23713 (4.7x). Both solutions are perfectly deterministic — zero variance across runs.
